title: China's YMTC Closes In on Micron and Kioxia in Global NAND Market
excerpt: Yangtze Memory Technologies has grown its NAND flash market share to 13% despite US export controls, narrowing the gap with established players and preparing for an IPO that could fuel further expansion.
body:
• YMTC's global NAND flash market share has risen to roughly 13% in Q1 2026, up from 8% a year ago, putting it nearly level with Micron (13.3%) and closing on Kioxia (15.9%)
  • The Chinese chipmaker is accelerating its third Wuhan fab, moving mass production forward from 2027 to H2 2026, with output projected to approach 2 million wafers this year
  • YMTC is preparing for a domestic IPO with a valuation expected to exceed $40 billion, which analysts say would give it the capital to surpass both Micron and Kioxia
  • Samsung leads the global NAND market at 30.4% revenue share, followed by SK Hynix at 16%, with AI demand driving record quarterly revenues across the sector

Rapid Market Share Gains Despite Sanctions

China's Yangtze Memory Technologies Co. (YMTC) has emerged as the most significant challenger to the established NAND flash memory hierarchy, steadily gaining market share despite US export controls designed to restrict China's access to advanced chipmaking equipment.

https://x.com/AlphaWireNewsAi/status/2087842714905928080

According to Counterpoint Research, YMTC's share of global NAND shipments reached approximately 13% in the first quarter of 2026, up from around 8% a year earlier. That puts the company nearly level with US-based Micron Technology, which holds 13.3% of the market by revenue, and within striking distance of Japan's Kioxia Holdings at 15.9%.

Samsung Electronics remains the dominant player with a 30.4% revenue share, followed by SK Hynix at 16%. But the competitive dynamics are shifting. NAND revenue across the industry surged approximately 3.5 times year-over-year in the most recent quarter, driven largely by AI-related demand for solid-state storage in data centers.

"If YMTC secures extra capital through this IPO, it will be fully equipped to scale up operations. Under this scenario, we expect YMTC to surpass both Kioxia and Micron to emerge as the world's No. 3 NAND player."

— MS Hwang, Research Director, Counterpoint Research

Production Expansion Accelerates

YMTC's growth has been fueled by aggressive capacity expansion. The company processed about 1.29 million wafers in 2024, rising to 1.77 million in 2025, with output projected to approach 2 million this year. By comparison, Samsung is expected to process about 4.7 million wafers and Kioxia about 4.69 million.

The company has accelerated the timeline for its third-phase fabrication plant in Wuhan, bringing forward expected mass production from 2027 to as early as the second half of 2026. The plant, which began construction in September 2025, is in the final stages of equipment installation. With its first and second fabs already operating at full capacity, the additional output is expected to significantly boost YMTC's global presence.

On the technology front, YMTC has narrowed the gap with market leaders. Its proprietary Xtacking 4.0 chip architecture runs at 270 layers, compared to SK Hynix's 321-layer 4D NAND and Samsung's 286-layer V-NAND. The company has launched products with 294-layer chips and is preparing to mass-produce NAND exceeding 300 layers later this year.

Price Advantage and Market Strategy

YMTC's growth has been driven by a volume-focused strategy and expansion into global consumer markets, including smartphones, PCs, and automotive applications. While its revenue share at roughly 11% trails its 13% shipment share, reflecting lower average selling prices, that price differential is itself a competitive weapon.

According to TechInsights, YMTC offers a 10-20% price edge over Japanese, Korean, and US rivals. Chinese manufacturers often enjoy a price advantage of more than 15% for products of the same specifications, making YMTC particularly attractive in price-sensitive general-purpose server and consumer markets.

The company's customer base includes major PC and storage brands such as Acer, Adata, Lexar, and Team Group, which use YMTC's NAND flash chips in their SSDs and storage devices. Domestic Chinese smartphone, notebook, and server companies have been key buyers, some benefiting from government subsidies for using local chips.

IPO and What It Means

YMTC has established a new entity with registered capital of 20.72 billion yuan (approximately $3 billion) and has officially begun its pre-listing regulatory review process for a domestic IPO. Its valuation is expected to exceed $40 billion.

The potential IPO would provide YMTC with additional capital to fund further expansion and technology development. Analysts at UBS have predicted the company will surpass Micron by early 2027 with roughly 14% market share.

For Micron, which generates nearly 80% of its revenue from DRAM — including the high-bandwidth memory critical for AI servers — YMTC's NAND growth is not an immediate threat to its core profit driver. But the shift is a reminder that the comfortable market structure enjoyed by established memory chipmakers is not permanent.

YMTC is also expanding into DRAM production, currently sampling low-power DRAM to customers. Three new plants under construction will have some capacity allocated to DRAM, with the exact proportion depending on development progress. The company's expansion into both NAND and DRAM positions it as an increasingly formidable competitor across the entire memory chip market.
